event.summary: Still-supported old-terminal recovery loses integration regression protection
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: existing old-terminal sessions are still supported at this revision, but their recovery from input-client failure, connection loss, a killed sink and supervisor death loses its distinguishing integration checks. This is a test-only coverage finding. No production failure was reproduced or inferred from execution. Revision of l1 after completed synthesis: the earlier proposed drop based on absence of a production defect is withdrawn; a test-only defect does not require an already-demonstrated runtime failure.

Intermediate source/contract: assigned 00802-001.patch:1-1000 removes input-client-failure/queued-output reattachment, connection-loss/queued-output reattachment, held natural-detach/takeover arbitration, killed-sink healing while both terminals answer, concurrent successful first-attach client counts, and real-supervisor-SIGKILL/stale-client cleanup scenarios. Patch lines 1001-1299 also retire their /proc diagnostic support and part of its test. SPEC_impl.md at 647f0227:2956-2962 says old tabs stay in tmux until closed and explicitly says, 'This path changes only for bug fixes.' The removed tests therefore still have a supported subject in that commit. The concrete lost assertions include replacement attach replying only after old input/output clients are gone; both attached terminals still answering after a real sink is killed; exactly five control clients for two attached terminals and one shared sink; and a fresh supervisor reaping two deliberately stale attached clients with queued output while the underlying session remains attachable. This record asserts the lost regression protection, not that the implementation violates those assertions.

Retained tests were checked rather than assumed equivalent. tmux/sink.rs:396-466 only establishes steady-state filtered-pane readability with and without a sink. service/terminals.rs:4068-4110 checks endless retries through a failing injected opener; 4172-4248 checks orderly process reaping and EOF-before-replacement with cat/sh stand-ins; 4690-4799 kills a cat-backed sink and checks retry timing, but subsequent opens fail. None proves successful real-tmux sink replacement leaves both attached terminals working under load. terminals.rs:3696-3798 gates two missing-session reservations and requires both opens to fail, so does not replace counting clients after two successful real attachments. The earlier registry/barrier seam checks at 3430-3690 protect lower-level ownership states, not queued-output transport failure through a live supervisor. tmux.rs:9377-9425 invokes reap_stale_control_clients after finding no server, requiring zero and no command invocation; it cannot distinguish omitting the positive stale-client reap. Symbol/caller searches found only that test call and the production startup call at core.rs:6447. Unchanged production identity arbitration, acknowledged no-output shutdown, barriers and reaping are not tests for their caller integration.

Later retirement is established, with its limits. The immediately following recorded commit dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4 changes the policy: SPEC_impl.md:2956-2967 says 'This release ends them at startup' and 'The running supervisor runs no tmux at all.' Its core.rs:6426-6438 actually calls OldTerminals::end_private_server before reload and then unconditionally tmux.no_server_after_startup(); core.rs:6965-6969 returns no terminal for every tmux-kind row. Thus the old-client/sink recovery subject is retired there even when the server-ending step fails; the supervisor no longer serves it. 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333 then removes the driver/sink implementation, and at pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db the searched sink/reap symbols are absent. This makes the old-terminal portion historical by tip, not an ongoing missing test for supported old-terminal recovery. It does not refute the gap at 647f0227.

The shared natural-detach arbitration survives the retirement and receives replacement protection later: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e introduces takeover_reason_wins_over_a_held_natural_detach in core/tests/host_terminals.rs (identified by git log -S). At tip, lines 3939-4047 hold a host input failure behind a Delete mark, take over, release arbitration, assert exactly one TakenOver notice, and verify winner output. It is absent by that name at 647f0227 and 1ed482d. Do not treat generic arbitration as an ongoing uncovered contract at tip.

Suggested bucket: other, because the established harm is lost regression protection in maintainer tests. Could-be-highest: no established catastrophic tooling, shipped security or user-work-loss consequence from this deletion; the original failure scenarios could threaten user sessions, but this finding establishes test loss only. Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis; no tests, builds or reproductions run. Proposed_drop: false. Parent decides whether subsequent retirement warrants exclusion; no drop is accepted by this record. Possible_cover: parent reports g152/l1 for migration integration protection lost at the same intermediate revision, and g151 for related lower-layer/process coverage questions. These may share a retirement rationale, but this group's input/connection/sink/crash recovery assertions are distinct from migration assertions; no coverage metadata or queued reports were read. Suggested remedy at the intermediate revision: retain or rehost the distinguishing real-tmux/supervisor regression cases until the support-removal commit, or keep that historical gap explicit in the review disposition. No unresolved source premise remains for this bounded coverage conclusion.
